result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A keeps the old list and pins visible for the whole load. It also says clearly when skeletons belong: only on first load or after a jump to a new area, when there's nothing old to show. B swaps the cards for skeletons after 1s, which throws away the previous results and partly defeats its own keep-the-old-results principle. B does have a slightly better map indicator (the 'Updating homes…' pill), and both handle failure well. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B keeps the old results on screen for the whole wait and limits skeletons to first loads or a jump to a new area, which handles both stale-content and layout-shift concerns well. Answer A swaps the cards for skeletons after 1s, which removes the old results during exactly the slow loads where they matter most and contradicts its own principle. Both answers treat failure well, and A's map pill gives a slightly clearer loading signal on the map.
